text:
[Previous context: The most recent - and interesting - estimates come from the] Global Burden of Disease Study 2010. This high-profile study estimated life expectancy at birth

for males in Vanuatu at 62.2 years in 2010 (with a 95 percent uncertainty interval range of 54.1

to 69.5 years) compared to life expectancy of 56 years at the time of Independence in 1980

(Wang H et al, 2012). Globally, a male life expectancy of 62.2 years is similar to that found in

the Federated States of Micronesia, Ghana, India, Lao PDR, Marshall Islands, Senegal, and

Seychelles. A Vanuatu male life expectancy of 62.2 years is higher than the average for Oceania

as a whole (58.8 years, although this average is brought down by just two countries: Papua New

Guinea (PNG) and Kiribati, where male life expectancy is 57.5 and 57.8 years, respectively) and

the Caribbean region (56.9 years). Vanuatu male life expectancy of 62.2 years is higher than in

the Solomon Islands (60.5 years) but lower than in Samoa (68.4 years), Tonga (67.3 years), or

Fiji (65.6 years). The Global Burden of Disease Study 2010 estimates paint a similar picture for

Vanuatu women: life expectancy is estimated at 66.9 years for females (59.8-72.5 years)
